_comment: Verified source register for the AI capability model. Governed by ADR-0010. Edited here. build/facts.py loads it; build.py check verifies that every citation string on a capability resolves through `normalize` (or `extra_from`) to an entry, and the provenance view reports grade exposure and locus coverage.

grades.A: openly available, dated, versioned, standards body or public authority
grades.B: openly available and dated, but vendor-published or non-normative
grades.C: available but undated / superseded / flagged historical / paywalled
grades.D: non-public, or not a publication at all - unusable as evidence externally

sources.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system
sources.locus_form: Clause number (e.g. 8.2) or Annex A control (e.g. A.5)
sources.caution: Paywalled: a reviewer without a licence cannot open it. EN ISO/IEC 42001:2026 is an identical European adoption, not a new edition.

sources.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence — AI system life cycle processes
sources.locus_form: Clause 6 process id (e.g. 6.4.8 AI data engineering)
sources.caution: Paywalled. 6.4.7 Knowledge acquisition, 6.4.8 AI data engineering and 6.4.14 Continuous validation are the AI-specific additions over ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288.

sources.title: Information technology — Governance of IT — Governance implications of the use of artificial intelligence by organizations
sources.locus_form: Clause number (e.g. 6.3 Governance of decision-making)
sources.caution: Paywalled. Our earlier short title paraphrased it — the canonical wording is 'by organizations', not 'for organizations'.

sources.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Guidance on risk management
sources.locus_form: Clause number (e.g. 6.4 Risk assessment)
sources.caution: Paywalled. Structure mirrors ISO 31000. The locus 6.4.2 Risk identification (7.3) was confirmed on 5 September 2026 against the standard's own table of contents in the publisher-authorized free preview (First edition, 2023-02, clause listed at page 11) - the clause body was not opened. Cite the clause number and title only; do not paraphrase or quote its content until a Bank licence holder reads it (OPEN-ITEMS item 11).

sources.title: Information technology — Artificial intelligence (AI) — AI system impact assessment
sources.locus_form: Clause number (e.g. 5.7 Establishing thresholds for sensitive uses)
sources.caution: Paywalled. Annex A gives the bridge to ISO/IEC 42001.

sources.title: Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection — Information security management systems — Requirements
sources.access: Paid — CHF 155; the 2024 climate amendment is free
sources.locus_form: Clause number or Annex A control (A.5 / A.6 / A.7 / A.8)
sources.caution: Paywalled. The 2022 edition renamed Annex A to 'Information security controls reference' — the 2013 wording no longer applies.

sources.title: Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection — Privacy information management systems — Requirements and guidance
sources.locus_form: Clause number (e.g. 8.2 Privacy risk assessment) or Annex A control
sources.caution: The 2025 second edition is a standalone management system standard; ISO/IEC 27701:2019 is withdrawn and its clause references no longer resolve. Annex F carries the correspondence.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.locus_form: Function, space, category.subcategory — e.g. GOVERN 1.1. NOT hyphenated
sources.caution: The hyphenated form GOVERN-1.1 is wrong; that convention belongs to AI 600-1 action ids (GV-1.1-001). Do not mix the two.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.locus_form: Named risk from clause 2 (e.g. Confabulation) or action id (e.g. GV-1.1-001)
sources.caution: A cross-sectoral profile of the AI RMF, not a standalone framework — always cite alongside S08.

sources.title: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449)
sources.locus_form: Section.Principle with trailing period — e.g. 1.3.
sources.caution: Cite the amended text. Principle 1.2 was retitled in 2024 — the 2019 name 'Human-centred values and fairness' is stale. Section 2 items are recommendations to adherents, not principles.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence: An Accountability Framework for Federal Agencies and Other Entities
sources.locus_form: Principle name (Governance / Data / Performance / Monitoring) plus the key practice wording
sources.caution: GAO uses no numbered clause identifiers, so a locus is a principle name plus practice text. GAO-23-106811 is testimony summarising this, not a replacement.

sources.title: AWS Cloud Adoption Framework for Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Generative AI
sources.locus_form: Perspective name (Business / People / Governance / Platform / Security / Operations) plus capability name
sources.caution: AWS now displays 'This whitepaper is for historical reference only.' Cite it as a February 2024 artifact and say so. It is our most-used vendor capability source.

sources.title: Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure — AI adoption
sources.locus_form: Phase name (Strategy / Plan / Ready / Govern / Secure / Manage)
sources.caution: Not a capability model and not a maturity model — there are no maturity levels and no capability taxonomy. Product-steering by design. Cite as a phase model only.

sources.title: Google Cloud's AI Adoption Framework
sources.locus_form: Theme name (Learn / Lead / Access / Scale / Secure / Automate) and epoch (Tactical / Strategic / Transformational)
sources.caution: Carries no date or version and says nothing about generative AI or agents. Genuinely a maturity grid, but do not present it as current.

sources.title: Generative AI Capability Model
sources.locus_form: Capability category name (e.g. GenAI Governance)
sources.caution: A solution/platform capability model, not an organizational one — not interchangeable with AWS CAF-AI. Category count renders as 6 or 7 across IBM's own paths; confirm on the citation date.

sources.title: NVIDIA Enterprise AI Factory Design Guide
sources.locus_form: Named section (e.g. Agentic AI in the Factory)
sources.caution: Cite the design guide on docs.nvidia.com, never the nvidia.com validated-design landing page, which is marketing collateral. Infrastructure layer only; hardware-prescriptive.

sources.title: SAP AI-native North Star architecture
sources.locus_form: Layer name (User Experience / Process / Foundation / Platform)
sources.caution: SAP's own disclaimer: 'This is not a specification, roadmap, or promise of delivery. It is a direction of travel.' Quote that if cited. SAP-product-scoped.

sources.title: The Agent Development Lifecycle: From Conception to Production
sources.locus_form: Phase name (Ideation and Design / Development / Testing and Validation / Deployment / Monitoring and Tuning)
sources.caution: No publication date exists — cite as undated, accessed on a stated day. Agentforce-scoped, so vendor-specific rather than an industry lifecycle.

sources.title: The AI-First Operating System: A Blueprint for Operating and Business Model Innovation
sources.publisher: World Economic Forum, in collaboration with Kearney
sources.locus_form: Building block name (Intelligence engines / Adaptive technology stacks / Operations redesign / Human-AI teaming / New value creation)
sources.caution: The only vendor-neutral source in the vendor group, which makes it useful for framing. Its five building blocks are conceptual groupings, not assessable capabilities — do not rest a gap assessment on it.

sources.title: The TOGAF Standard, 10th Edition
sources.access: Free for non-commercial after registration; paid for commercial
sources.locus_form: Named Fundamental Content document plus section (e.g. Architecture Content, §33.2.4)
sources.caution: The 10th Edition is six Fundamental Content documents plus a Library of Series Guides, not one book with Parts I-VI. Open Group publication URLs increasingly sit behind SSO — check the link resolves on the day you publish.

sources.title: Capability-Based Planning: Supporting Project/Portfolio and Digital Capabilities Mapping Using the TOGAF and ArchiMate Standards
sources.locus_form: Series Guide reference - G193 for capability-based planning, G211 for business capabilities
sources.caution: REPLACES our earlier citation of 'TOGAF (capability-based planning)'. Chapter 28 of TOGAF 9.2 was deliberately REMOVED in the 10th Edition; capability-based planning is not a section of the current Standard. For business capabilities themselves cite G211 (Business Capabilities, Version 2, April 2022), which supersedes G189 - NOT G190, which is Information Mapping.

sources.title: The Open Group Open Agile Architecture Standard, Version 2.0
sources.access: Free perpetual non-commercial licence; paid commercial
sources.locus_form: Part name (The Agile Way of Thinking / The Agile Enterprise / The Agile Architecture Capability / The Ways of Supporting)
sources.caution: v2.0 restructured the Parts — v1.0 (C208, 2020) part names do not apply. The publication year is not rendered on The Open Group's announcement page; confirm from the document cover.

sources.title: The Open Group IT4IT Standard, Version 3.0.1
sources.locus_form: Value stream name (Evaluate / Explore / Integrate / Deploy / Release / Consume / Operate)
sources.caution: v3.0 replaced the four v2.x value streams (Strategy to Portfolio, Requirement to Deploy, Request to Fulfill, Detect to Correct). Those names are superseded — do not use them.

sources.title: ITIL 4
sources.locus_form: Practice name, or Service Value Chain activity
sources.caution: ITIL Version 5 was announced January 2026 and is rolling out; ITIL 4 remains valid in parallel through a transition period. A 2026 deliverable citing ITIL 4 as THE current ITIL needs that qualifier. Not freely readable.

sources.title: Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM)
sources.locus_form: Component name plus capability number
sources.caution: Available exclusively to member firms, so a reviewer outside the membership cannot verify a citation. 8 components / 34 capabilities / 101 sub-capabilities.

sources.title: AI, Data & Analytics Controls (ADAC)
sources.locus_form: None — nothing citable exists
sources.caution: REMOVE. ADAC is a workgroup, absent from EDM Council's own Frameworks page; evidence of activity is webinars and a 2024 SIG deck. If an EDM Council AI/data-controls reference is needed, cite CDMC, which is openly available.

sources.title: The FinOps Framework
sources.locus_form: Domain name plus capability name (e.g. Optimize Usage & Cost — Rate Optimization)
sources.caution: 'FinOps for AI' is a named Technology Category with nine AI-specific KPIs; 'AI for FinOps' is a different topic. Do not conflate the two in a citation.

sources.title: Assurance and Advice in Support of Effective Governance: Three Lines Model Statement of Position
sources.locus_form: Principle number (1-5), or Part I / Part II
sources.caution: REPLACES the 2020 position paper, which The IIA marks superseded. The 2026 Statement has FIVE principles, not six. 'Three Lines of Defense' is doubly retired — do not use it.

sources.title: The MITRE AI Maturity Model and Organizational Assessment Tool Guide
sources.access: Free — guide only; assessment tool on request
sources.locus_form: Pillar name (Ethical, Equitable, and Responsible Use / Strategy and Resources / Organization / Technology Enablers / Data / Performance and Application)
sources.caution: Six pillars, 20 dimensions, five levels (Initial / Adopted / Defined / Managed / Optimized). Pre-dates the generative-AI wave — defensible as a maturity reference, not as current AI guidance.

sources.title: Grow Enterprise AI Maturity for Bottom-Line Impact (MIT CISR Research Briefing, Vol. XXV, No. 8)
sources.publisher: MIT Sloan Center for Information Systems Research
sources.access: Readable on site; PDF requires login
sources.locus_form: Briefing volume and number, plus stage name
sources.caution: 'MIT CISR' is a research centre, not a document — our earlier citation named no artifact. This briefing is the correct substitute: four stages (Experiment and Prepare / Build Pilots and Capabilities / Develop AI Ways of Working / Become AI Future Ready).

sources.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
sources.publisher: IMDA Singapore and AI Verify Foundation
sources.locus_form: Dimension name (one of nine, e.g. Content Provenance)
sources.status: Current — but our citation was ambiguous
sources.caution: THREE documents share this name: the original (2nd ed. 2020), the Generative AI framework (May 2024, nine dimensions) and the Agentic AI framework (v1.0, January 2026, four dimensions). Our model cited it unqualified. Pick one per capability.

sources.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
sources.locus_form: Dimension name (one of four)
sources.caution: Added during this review as the correct source for agentic capabilities previously attributed to the generative-AI framework. Supersession check 9 September 2026: IMDA published an update dated 20 May 2026 incorporating industry feedback, adding best practices and case studies on multi-agent systems, third-party agents and automation bias. The IMDA factsheet page carrying that date was opened; the updated framework body was not. The register previously recorded only the 22 January 2026 launch.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 (OWASP GenAI Security Project)
sources.locus_form: Entry NAME, never the number (e.g. Excessive Agency)
sources.caution: Item numbers change between editions — cite by name only. The owasp.org/www-project-top-10-for-large-language-model-applications page was still serving the 2025 list; do not cite that URL. Also under this project: Agent Control Standard, Top 10 for Agentic Applications.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol Specification
sources.publisher: Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation); originated at Anthropic
sources.locus_form: Dated revision plus section (e.g. 2026-07-28, Server Features)
sources.caution: Breaking revision: sessions and the initialize handshake removed, server/discover added, Roots, Sampling and Logging deprecated. Architecture text written against 2025-11-25 or earlier is out of date. Governance moved to the Linux Foundation in December 2025 — cite AAIF, not Anthropic.

sources.title: Gartner research (various)
sources.locus_form: Document number only, in internal documents only
sources.caution: Licensed material. Usable internally under the Bank's subscription; must not appear in deliverables that circulate externally, and a reviewer without a seat cannot open it. Cannot serve as evidence.

sources.title: Consultancy transformation patterns (unattributed)
sources.locus_form: None — nothing citable exists
sources.caution: REMOVE or replace. An unattributed pattern is not evidence; it cannot be opened, dated or verified by anyone.

sources.title: IDB internal practice (undocumented)
sources.locus_form: Name the internal document, owner and date
sources.caution: Legitimate as an origin, but 'institutional practice' names nothing a reviewer can open. Each use must be replaced with a named internal policy, standard or procedure with an owner and a date.

sources.title: IDB data protection framework
sources.locus_form: Name the instrument and clause
sources.caution: Data Governance to confirm the instrument name, version and the specific provision relied on.

sources.title: IDB legal framework
sources.locus_form: Name the instrument and clause
sources.caution: Legal to confirm which instrument is relied on. Related: the obligations register (18 statutory references, all still marked candidate).

sources.title: IDB internal audit standards
sources.locus_form: Name the instrument and clause
sources.caution: Internal Audit to confirm which standards are relied on and whether the IIA Global Internal Audit Standards (2024) are adopted directly.

sources.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
sources.publisher: Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation; donated by Google, 2025)
sources.locus_form: Named concept or section (e.g. Agent Card, Task lifecycle)
sources.caution: Verified 9 September 2026: the specification page states 'Latest Released Version 1.0.0' and governance by the Agentic AI Foundation. The v1.0 release date of 12 March 2026 comes from a secondary source and is NOT verified. Graded A for consistency with S33 (MCP), which is the same character of artifact.

sources.title: Software and systems engineering — Software testing — Part 11: Guidelines on the testing of AI-based systems
sources.locus_form: Clause number (e.g. 7 Testing of AI-based systems)
sources.caution: Paywalled and a Technical Report, not a normative standard. Predates generative AI (2020). Cited for the test-oracle problem and non-determinism, which is what makes trajectory evaluation impossible to run as a golden-dataset exercise. Title, number and date confirmed against the ISO catalogue page on 9 September 2026; body not opened.

sources.title: Software engineering — Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Quality model for AI systems
sources.locus_form: Clause number, or quality characteristic name
sources.caution: Paywalled. ISO/IEC DIS 25059 ('Quality models for AI systems') is in ballot, so a revision is in flight — re-check before relying on a clause. Title, number and the existence of the DIS confirmed against the ISO catalogue on 9 September 2026; body not opened.

sources.title: Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models: An SSDF Community Profile
sources.locus_form: SSDF practice or task id (e.g. PW.4, PO.1.1)
sources.caution: Augments SP 800-218 (SSDF v1.1) with AI-specific practices across the development life cycle. Publication, status and date confirmed against NIST/CSRC on 9 September 2026; body not opened, so no practice id is pinned.

sources.title: Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) Specification
sources.access: Open; the identical ISO adoption is paid
sources.locus_form: Section name, or the SCI formula term
sources.caution: Adopted as ISO/IEC 21031:2024, which is paywalled; cite the openly readable GSF specification and note the ISO adoption. SCI is a rate per functional unit, which is why it fits 6.5.3's shape — a token is a natural functional unit. Publisher page and the ISO adoption confirmed 9 September 2026; specification body not opened.

OWASP GenAI Security Project - agent con.locus: Agent Control Standard (donated to the project, announced 2026-09-01) - UNVERIFIED: structure and control set not opened
